description: Source-lore pass 16 upgrades all five airship core entries and imports non-Elven operation, ship tracking, and the Culverin and Skysea chase narrative.

entries.title: Dwarven Airship Core
entries.summary: Dwarven cores are heavy cylindrical engines forged from sturdy metals, enchanted crystals, and runic mechanical systems for reliable long-term lift.
body: Dwarven cores are compact relative to their power but physically heavy and robust. Thick cylindrical chambers and reinforcing appendages are designed to survive structural strain and to support vessels ranging from personal craft to floating fortresses.

Foundries combine blacksmithing, artifice, enchantment, magical ores, fire-infused crystals, and enchanted molten metals. This labor and material burden makes the cores expensive and closely tied to Dwarven strongholds and guild halls.
Controlled geothermal or elemental combustion creates heated lift and fire-driven thrust. The result is consistent, durable, long-lived power with less agility than lighter traditions.
Large vessels link multiple cores into an interconnected system capable of lifting enormous cargo, castles, industrial platforms, and dreadnoughts.

sections.heading: Legacy Cost Scale
body: The source prices small cores in the thousands of gold and large industrial cores in the tens of thousands. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Elven Airship Core
entries.summary: Elven cores are sacred luminous crystalline conduits that draw from the Weave and form a continuous magical bond with their operators.
body: Elven cores are living or responsive magical entities rather than ordinary engines. A luminous crystal or faceted gemstone sits within delicate enchanted wood or metal latticework, matching the elegance of the vessel around it.

Creation combines rare natural materials, elemental crystals, precious wood and metal, ancient rites, and high arcane mastery. Each core is attuned to the Weave and to an approved operator, making it artwork, sacred object, and strategic technology at once.

The operator channels magical essence through constant physical and spiritual contact to regulate lift and propulsion. Small ships may need one bonded operator; great vessels and floating fortresses require several acting in harmony.
Their grace, fine control, and maneuverability carry strict cultural and operational constraints. Possessing or operating one without Fae approval can become a diplomatic and spiritual offense.

sections.heading: Legacy Cost Scale
body: The source places even basic Elven cores in the tens of thousands of gold and makes price depend on size and intricacy. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Non-Elven Operation of Elven Cores
entries.summary: Non-Elven operators can sometimes maintain passive flotation or force an Elven core into flight, but face unstable energy, constant concentration, exhaustion, backlash, and catastrophic descent.
body: Elven cores are intrinsically aligned with Fae affinity for the Weave. Outsiders lack the natural synchronization that makes energy flow smooth, so power fluctuates, surges, falls dormant, or feeds back into ship and operator.
Passive mode can keep a ship floating without propulsion, but it still requires repeated magical attention. Neglect drains the core and begins a slow descent.

Active flight demands continuous regulation of propulsion, direction, altitude, and sudden maneuvers. The operator must supply personal magical energy and concentration, making long operation physically and mentally exhausting.

Failure can cause erratic rises and drops, loss of propulsion, force backlash, magical burnout, loss of spellcasting capacity, nosedives, shutdown, or total core deactivation. Continued operation without a bonded Elven crew is therefore an emergency measure, not a stable replacement.

sections.heading: Legacy Operation Checks
body: The source specifies six-hour passive checks, escalating Arcana DCs for basic, advanced, and emergency operation, fatigue saves, force damage, descent rates, shutdown durations, and critical failure. Conversion is required.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Adversity for Non-Elven Operators of Elven Airship Cores

entries.title: Dragon Kin Airship Core
entries.summary: Dragon Kin cores bind breath gems, scales, draconic metals, runes, and elemental force into large majestic engines of lift and destruction.
body: Dragon Kin cores mirror draconic heritage through force, majesty, and elemental power. Large hexagonal or octagonal housings bear scale motifs and durable draconic metals.

Manufacture uses breath gems, enchanted scales, ancient dragon runes, dangerous binding rituals, and elemental forces such as fire or lightning. Rare materials and dragonblood magic make the process exceptionally expensive.

Controlled releases of breath-like energy produce lift and thrust through explosive channels. Small cores power agile ships; larger cores can lift dreadnoughts, fortresses, and immense masses through raw elemental potency.

sections.heading: Legacy Cost Scale
body: The source prices small cores near Elven-core levels and great cores in the tens of thousands of gold. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Gnomish Airship Core
entries.summary: Gnomish cores combine portable clockwork mechanisms, gears, levers, crystals, arcane circuitry, steam, and compressed air for fine control and customization.
body: Gnomish cores are compact, spherical or boxlike networks of precision mechanisms and enchanted crystals. Some are small enough to be carried by one person.

Rare metals, clockwork components, runes, and magical circuitry are assembled through repeated experimentation. Constant refinement means individual cores differ from one another and often require specialized knowledge.

Mechanical precision and arcane enhancement provide quick adjustments in movement and direction. Small units suit scouts and private craft; larger systems can lift factories, clockwork cities, and experimental heavy vessels.

sections.heading: Legacy Cost Scale
body: The source places personal cores in the thousands of gold with larger models costing substantially more. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Human Airship Core
entries.summary: Human cores are affordable patchwork hybrids of Dwarven mechanics and Gnomish arcana, built quickly from practical, scavenged, and mass-produced components.
body: Human cores combine heavy mechanical principles with arcane-infused gears, crystals, pistons, vents, and conduits. Their exposed industrial construction is bulky, noisy, varied, and often visibly improvised.

Busy workshops and makeshift factories use available metals, scavenged enchantments, and rudimentary binding methods. Faster production and adaptable materials lower cost but create inconsistent efficiency and reliability.

Steam-powered pistons and elemental magic generate lift and thrust. Small cores serve personal and cargo craft, while linked multicore systems can support merchant fleets, battlecruisers, and small fortresses at the price of frequent fuel and maintenance.

sections.heading: Legacy Cost Scale
body: The source prices small Human cores in the hundreds of gold and larger systems in the thousands, varying by quality and modification. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Tracking an Airship
entries.summary: Airships are tracked through visual signs, smoke, cloud disruption, ether trails, magical beacons, elemental disturbances, radar, sonar, thermal differences, and coordinated pursuit.
body: Tracking begins by selecting a method suited to the target and conditions. Visual trackers follow smoke, reflections, silhouettes, and disturbed clouds. Arcane trackers read ether trails, beacons, or elemental residue. Mechanical operators use radar, sonar, and heat differences.

Weather, darkness, cloud density, distance, magical interference, and evasive maneuvers determine whether contact can be maintained. Targets can hide in storms, break line of sight, deploy stealth runes, cloak themselves, or exploit currents and terrain.
Specialized sensors, trained mages, multiple simultaneous methods, and allied tracking ships improve pursuit. Long chases strain crews and equipment, and repeated failure loses the trail.
A maintained track reveals periodic location and heading. Closing to interception distance shifts the contest from detection to piloting, engagement, or boarding.

sections.heading: Legacy Tracking Procedure
body: The source provides Perception, Arcana, and Investigation checks, distance rolls, ten-minute intervals, escalating DCs, smoke, ether, radar and sonar scenarios, critical results, fatigue, teamwork, stealth, trail loss, and interception checks. Conversion is required.

entries.title: The Chase Over the Culverin and Skysea
entries.summary: An Elven Skyguard account describes the Dawnrider hunting the human smuggling vessel Chameleon through magical fog between Telverid Island and Morrison Lookout.
body: Captain Elion's Elven vessel, the Dawnrider, pursued the human Chameleon from Telverid Island toward Morrison Lookout. Lieutenant Taelis led tracking efforts as the smugglers used smoke, currents, fog banks, cloaking, and weather manipulation to hide a slower ship from faster Elven hunters.

The pursuit became a contest of patience. The Dawnrider avoided pressing so hard that the Chameleon would break clear and maneuver away, instead allowing the humans to believe they could escape deeper into cloud cover where dense currents slowed them.

Magically thick fog defeated both visual and arcane tracking for a time. A brief shimmer exposed the Chameleon's attempt to accelerate out of concealment. The Elven crew closed to half a mile, surged through the fog, and fired into its sails.

The human captain surrendered rather than risk another volley, boarding casualties, diplomatic escalation, or a fall into the abyss. The Chameleon's crew outnumbered the Elves, but speed, positioning, and the forced choice between concealment and escape decided the chase.
